title: Dependability campaign orchestration canvas — cross-team SLO rollout
body:
Purpose:
This canvas captures a pragmatic, cross-functional orchestration plan to roll out a standardized dependability program across product teams. Unlike a one-off SLO checklist, this campaign treats SLOs as a product change: we will instrument, measure, iterate, and automate enforcement policies over three progressive phases. The goal is to reduce customer-visible incidents by 30% for targeted services while clarifying ownership and creating reproducible playbooks.

Background & motivation:
- Several services have divergent SLO practices: some teams have ad hoc error budgets, others have no defined SLOs.
- Incidents over the past 12 months show recurring contributor patterns (cache misses, suboptimal batching, retry storms).
- Executive priority: demonstrable reliability improvements for paid hosted customers and Dedicated deployments.

Campaign hypothesis:
If we systematically align teams on a common SLO taxonomy, close instrumentation gaps, and run three progressive enforcement experiments (observability -> guardrails -> automated fallback), then we will reduce customer-facing degradations and shorten mean time to mitigation.

Scope (initial pilot):
- Target services: inference-routing, kv-cache, auth/quotas, and streaming proxy.
- Excluded: model training pipelines, offline analytics.
- Duration: 16 weeks from kickoff (pilot), with phase gates to expand.

Core objectives (success criteria):
- Define and publish SLOs (latency p50/p95, availability, error-rate) for each pilot service within 3 weeks.
- Achieve complete signal coverage (traces, metrics, alerts) for 80% of critical SLOs by week 8.
- Reduce customer-impacting incident frequency by 30% over 12 weeks post-rollout for pilot services.
- Establish standard runbook and automated escalation for each SLO.

Stakeholders & RACI (high level):
- Product (observable SLIs and customer impact definitions) — Responsible: Priya Sharma, Accountable: Product Lead.
- SRE — Responsible: Asha R. Patel, Accountable: SRE Manager.
- Serving Runtime Eng — Consulted: Marcus Li (latency signal owners).
- Platform Eng (deploy & routing) — Consulted: Diego Alvarez.
- Developer Experience / Console — Informed/Responsible for dashboards: Ellen Cho.
- Security & Compliance — Informed (data retention/PII in traces).

SLO taxonomy (standardized template):
- SLO name (short): e.g., inference-routing-success-rate
- Consumer impact statement: "Requests that return a usable completion to end-users within 3000ms"
- SLI(s): success_rate, latency_p95_ms, streaming_stall_rate
- Objective: target (e.g., success_rate >= 99.5% over 30-day rolling window)
- Error budget: 100% - target = allowed errors per 30 days
- Measurement window: rolling 30d and 7d for alarm thresholds

Instrumentation & gaps (discovery snapshot):
- Traces: present end-to-end for ~60% of flows; missing for batch-prefetch path.
- Metrics: p50/p95 latencies exist but not tagged by customer_tier or route.
- Logs: structured, but sampling rules drop low-frequency error variants.
- Action: week 1–4 workstreams to add route tagging, enable finer trace sampling for suspect paths, and add a per-tenant telemetry flag for Dedicated customers.

Milestone plan (16-week pilot):
- Week 0: Kickoff, alignment workshop, SLO taxonomy finalization, owner assignment.
- Week 1–3: Define SLOs, instrument missing metrics, update schema for route tags.
- Week 4–6: Dashboard templates (Console), create baseline reports, run initial chaos probes (low blast radius).
- Week 7–8: Error budget experiments phase 1 (manual guardrails): pages/alerts on 7d burn, team war-room rehearsals.
- Week 9–11: Phase 2: automated mitigations (traffic reroute to fallback model variant, KV cache priming), require feature flags for quick rollback.
- Week 12–14: Phase 3: progressive enforcement (quota throttles for noisy tenants, automated rate limiters), postmortem automation.
- Week 15–16: Pilot retrospective, playbook publication, decision gate to scale to additional services.

Experiment playbooks (concise):
- Observability experiment: enable fine-grained traces for 1% of traffic for 2 weeks, compare error-class distribution pre/post.
- Guardrail experiment: create 7d burn alert -> trigger a manual incident runbook for the owning team. Measure time-to-detect and time-to-restore.
- Automated mitigation experiment: on p95 latency breach for 10 minutes, reroute 10% traffic to a lower-cost but compatible model endpoint; measure degradation vs. customer impact.

Dashboards & alerts (early design):
- Console SLO page: unified SLO card (target, current burn, projection) + quick link to recent incidents and runbook.
- Team dashboard: partitionable by route, cluster, customer_tier.
- Pager rules: primary alert on projected error budget exhaustion within 7 days; secondary on anomalous spike in p95 latency or client error rates.

Runbooks & escalation:
- Every SLO must have an attached one-page runbook: owner, diagnosis checklist (network, backpressure, hotshard, KV miss), mitigation knobs, rollback steps, postmortem template.
- War-room checklist for first 60 minutes, and decision criteria for declaring severity levels.

Training & org readiness:
- SRE-driven half-day hands-on session (week 6) for each participating team: walk through runbooks and playbook drills.
- Post-training mini-exercise (week 8): simulated runaway retries with injected traces to validate detection.

Communication & change management:
- Weekly cross-functional sync (30m) during pilot, recorded notes to Confluence.
- Executive update at week 8 and final results at week 16.
- Customer comms: for Dedicated customers in pilot, share baseline SLOs and expected impact; include opt-in telemetry flag.

Risk register (top items) and mitigations:
- Risk: instrumentation changes add latency or noise. Mitigation: sample at low rate first, measure overhead.
- Risk: automated mitigations may surface unexpected degradations. Mitigation: canary the mitigation and require feature-flag gating.
- Risk: disparate definitions of "usable completion" across products. Mitigation: product workshop to align consumer-facing definitions and map to metrics.

Resource estimate (engineering effort):
- SRE: 0.5 FTE for 16 weeks (coordination, runbooks, training)
- Serving runtime: 1.0 FTE (instrumentation, mitigation hooks)
- Console/DevX: 0.5 FTE (dashboards, SLO templates)
- Product/PM: 0.2 FTE (definitions, stakeholder alignment)
- QA/Oncall rotation: incremental test and run coverage adjustments.

Acceptance criteria to graduate pilot:
- Published SLOs and runbooks for each pilot service.
- Instrumentation coverage >= 80% for defined SLIs.
- Demonstrable reduction in customer-visible incidents (target >= 20% improvement in first month after enforcement) or clear path documented to reach 30% within 12 weeks.
- Playbook and dashboard artifacts committed to the shared Confluence + repo and listed linked_artifacts.

Open questions & next steps (owner tags):
- Q: Should SLO objectives be uniform across Hosted vs Dedicated? (Owner: Product, Priya)
- Q: Which tenant-labeling strategy minimizes cardinality while preserving per-tenant signal? (Owner: Serving Runtime, Marcus)
- Next 7 days: schedule kickoff, complete SLO template draft, inventory instrumentation owners (Owner: Asha).

Notes / heuristics learned from prior efforts (short):
- Start small: pick one high-visibility route and make it exemplary; the rest follow by pattern.
- Automate measurement early: projections are more persuasive than post-hoc summaries.
- Use error budget burn as a collaborative SLA, not a punitive quota: tie to joint remediation goals.

Appendix (quick links to templates):
- SLO template: copy into Confluence at CONFL-3492-dependability-canvas
- Runbook template: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/runbooks/template.md

Prepared by: Asha R. Patel (SRE)
Reviewers: Marcus Li (Serving Runtime), Priya Sharma (Product), Diego Alvarez (Platform)
